# Ship History
[italic]A short history of the USCSS Daybreak for anyone who woke up aboard her, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## A Company Hull The Daybreak was built as a commercial starship, and the USCSS on her bow still says so. She was laid out for freight and for the people who move it: two hangars, a flight deck, a cargo lift and racks of containers stencilled for Weyland-Yutani and Trijent. Some of those containers have not been opened in years, and nobody aboard is quite sure what is in them.
## Under Charter Like a lot of Company hulls on the frontier, she now flies under charter to government forces. The refit was practical rather than pretty: - A [bold]Combat Information Center[/bold] went in where the old operations room stood, with sensor and mapping consoles bolted to the deck. - A [bold]brig[/bold] was walled off near the command spaces. The crew will tell you it is rarely empty. - The hangars took on an armoured personnel carrier, a fabricator for the dropships and a stack of ammunition no Company inspector would sign for. - The hypersleep bay was kept. Most of the detachment travels frozen, and wakes up when the work starts.
## Who Is Aboard The Daybreak carries a detachment of riflemen, corpsmen, pilots, radio operators and officers, along with the engineers who keep the fusion plant honest and the hands who run the galley. On paper she belongs to the Company. In practice she goes where her charter sends her, and the people aboard rarely hear why before they arrive.
## The Herald Aboard A ship is a small town with no roads out. Rumour moves faster than air through the vents, and orders arrive without reasons. The Herald keeps a correspondent aboard for the same reason we keep one on any colony: so that when something happens out here, somebody writes down who was there and what was done.
We keep the archive in the ship's net and send a copy home with every relay packet, so it outlasts the charter.
